# Command panel

Every line below is a command the server understands. Each one gets a **code
lens** above it (click it), a **code action** when the cursor is on it, and
**completion** inside the fence — put the cursor on a blank line in the block
and ask for completions to see the catalogue.

```oysterlsp
daily/today
daily/yesterday
daily/tomorrow
daily/prev
daily/next
```

Two of them are missing a clickable lens here, and that is the feature
working: `daily/prev` and `daily/next` are answered *relative to the note the
block sits in*, and this note is not a daily note. Their lenses say so instead
of disappearing. Open [[2026-07-26]] to see the same two lines come alive.

## The catalogue

| Line | Does |
|---|---|
| `daily/today` | Open today's daily note, creating it when missing |
| `daily/yesterday` | Open yesterday's daily note, creating it when missing |
| `daily/tomorrow` | Open tomorrow's daily note, creating it when missing |
| `daily/prev` | Open the previous existing daily note, relative to this note |
| `daily/next` | Open the next existing daily note, relative to this note |

This table and the block above are both generated from
`Lsp_lib.Command_block.all_of_command`, so they cannot drift from what the
server actually accepts.

## Try breaking it

An unrecognized line is a diagnostic, not silence — see [[diagnostics]].

## Try writing one

Open a note with no block at all — [[anchors]] — and ask for code actions
anywhere in it: *Insert oysterlsp command block*. It writes only the commands
that can run in that note.
